title: Generalized Holstein-Primakoff transformation with optimizable bosonic truncation
authors: Yang Liu, Jia-Wei Mei, Rong Yu, Z. Y. Xie, Hong-Gang Luo, Jize Zhao
abstract: Spin-wave theory provides a quasiparticle description of excitation spectra in quantum spin systems. In this theory, the spin operators are usually bosonized by the Holstein-Primakoff transformation or the Dyson-Maleev transformation. In practical calculations, the bosonized Hamiltonian has to be truncated, and thus the resulting excitation spectra depend on the choice of bosonic representation. Here, we introduce a generalized Holstein-Primakoff transformation that continuously interpolates between the conventional Holstein-Primakoff and Dyson-Maleev transformations through a single parameter. The formulation naturally extends to the SU(N) algebra and provides a flexible framework for optimizing bosonic truncations beyond harmonic order. As an application, we investigate the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic model on the square lattice. By combining the generalized Holstein-Primakoff transformation with continuous similarity transformations, we obtain excitation spectra in excellent agreement with tensor-network calculations. Our results demonstrate that optimizing the bosonic representation substantially reduces truncation errors and provides quantitatively reliable descriptions of both quasiparticle dispersions and multi-boson continua.
summary: The paper develops a generalized Holstein-Primakoff transformation that offers a flexible way to optimize bosonic truncations in spin-wave theory. By tuning an interpolation parameter, the authors significantly reduce approximation errors when studying models like the BBH Hamiltonian on a square lattice. The optimized results show excellent quantitative agreement with advanced tensor-network calculations for key magnetic excitations.
main_problem: Spin-wave theory requires bosonizing spin operators, but the resulting Hamiltonian must be truncated, leading to results dependent on the chosen bosonic representation.
main_result: A generalized Holstein-Primakoff transformation allows continuous optimization of the bosonic truncation parameter, substantially reducing errors and yielding quantitative agreement with tensor-network calculations for excitation spectra.
method: The authors introduce a generalized HP transformation parameterized by $x$ that interpolates between known transformations. They optimize this representation by minimizing the ground-state energy or matching spectral features against highly accurate tensor-network benchmarks.
model_or_system: The primary application is to the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic (BBH) model on a square lattice, particularly in the ferroquadrupolar phase. The theory extends to $	ext{SU}(N)$ algebras and utilizes automatic differentiation for implementation.
key_observables: Excitation spectra (quasiparticle dispersions), dynamical spin structure factors ($\mathcal{A}_{k\omega}$), and ground-state energy ($E_g$).
important_parameters: The interpolation parameter $x$ ($0 \le x \le 1$), the coupling constants defining the BBH model, and the lattice momentum $\mathbf{k}$.
main_assumptions: The accuracy of spin-wave theory is limited by the finite order of truncation; however, optimizing the representation mitigates this dependence.
figures_summary: Figures compare quadrupolar mode dispersion ($\omega$ vs $k$) and spectral functions between optimized Continuous Similarity Transformation (CST) results and Tensor Network (TN) calculations, showing excellent quantitative agreement, especially reproducing interaction-induced roton minima.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the generalized HP transformation and its extension to $	ext{SU}(N)$. It then applies this framework to the spin-1 BBH model on a square lattice, comparing results derived from optimized GSWT against established TN benchmarks for excitation spectra and spectral functions.
why_interesting: This work provides a systematic, tunable theoretical tool (the generalized HP transformation) to improve quantitative accuracy in strongly correlated magnetic systems by optimizing the underlying mathematical representation used in mean-field approximations.
